cities.name: Moscow

seo.title: Moscow Travel Guide: Red Square, Kremlin & Museums
seo.description: Explore Moscow’s Red Square, Kremlin, St Basil’s Cathedral, Tretyakov Gallery and Bolshoi Theatre. History, tips and a 4-day itinerary.
seo.h1: Moscow Travel Guide: Kremlin, Red Square and Russian Art

cities.heading: Moscow Travel Guide: Kremlin, Red Square and Russian Art
overview: Moscow is Russia’s political and historical centre. It developed around the Kremlin and became the capital of the Soviet Union and the modern Russian Federation.

The city’s core is arranged in rings around the Kremlin, with historic churches, monasteries, Soviet-era landmarks and modern parks. The Moscow Metro is known for decorated stations that function as public art.

quickFacts.bestTime: May–September; winters are cold and snowy
quickFacts.knownFor: Kremlin, Red Square, St Basil’s, museums, theatre

places.name: Red Square
places.description: Russia’s most famous public square, surrounded by the Kremlin, St Basil’s Cathedral, GUM department store and the State Historical Museum. It is part of the UNESCO-listed Kremlin and Red Square.
places.visitorTip: Visit early morning or evening for photographs; some areas close for events.

places.name: Moscow Kremlin
places.description: A fortified complex that includes cathedrals, palaces and the Armoury Chamber, combining medieval Russian, Orthodox, imperial and state architecture. It is also a working government complex, so access is limited to some areas.
places.visitorTip: Book tickets for the cathedral square and Armoury Chamber in advance.

places.name: St Basil’s Cathedral
places.description: Built between 1555 and 1561 under Ivan the Terrible, its colourful onion domes form one of Russia’s most recognisable silhouettes. It is formally called the Cathedral of the Intercession on the Moat.
places.visitorTip: Interior is small; allow 30–45 minutes.

places.name: Tretyakov Gallery
places.description: Founded in 1856 by Pavel Tretyakov, it is the leading museum of Russian national art, with icons and paintings from medieval to modern times.
places.visitorTip: Visit the main gallery in Lavrushinsky Lane for classical works.

places.name: Bolshoi Theatre
places.description: One of the world’s most famous institutions for Russian ballet and opera, in a neoclassical building that reopened in 2011 after renovation.
places.visitorTip: Book performance tickets well ahead.

places.name: Gorky Park and Zaryadye Park
places.description: Gorky Park and Zaryadye Park by the Kremlin demonstrate Moscow’s contemporary public-space development, with walks, events and river views.
places.visitorTip: Walk along the Moscow River in summer.

cities.name: Saint Petersburg

seo.title: Saint Petersburg Travel Guide: Hermitage & Palaces
seo.description: Discover Saint Petersburg: the Hermitage, Peterhof, Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood, St Isaac’s and Nevsky Prospekt. Tips and itinerary.
seo.h1: Saint Petersburg Travel Guide: Imperial Palaces and Museums

cities.heading: Saint Petersburg Travel Guide: Imperial Palaces and Museums
overview: Saint Petersburg was founded by Peter the Great in 1703 and served as Russia’s imperial capital for more than two centuries. It was planned as a European-style city of canals, palaces, avenues and monumental public buildings.
The Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments is a UNESCO World Heritage property, which includes major Baroque and Neoclassical landmarks.

quickFacts.bestTime: June–August (White Nights); winter for snowy scenery
quickFacts.knownFor: Hermitage, imperial palaces, canals, White Nights

places.name: Hermitage Museum and Winter Palace
places.description: The Hermitage grew from Catherine the Great’s collection in the 18th century and occupies the Baroque Winter Palace. It holds millions of objects from Europe, Asia, Egypt, Greece and Russia.
places.visitorTip: Buy tickets online and plan a focused route.

places.name: Peterhof Palace
places.description: A grand palace-and-park complex begun in 1714 and inspired partly by Versailles, famed for the Grand Cascade and golden fountains.
places.visitorTip: Fountains operate seasonally (roughly late spring to early autumn).

places.name: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
places.description: Built between 1883 and 1907 on the site where Alexander II was assassinated, with Russian Revival architecture and extensive interior mosaics.
places.visitorTip: Allow 45 minutes to see the mosaics.

places.name: St Isaac’s Cathedral
places.description: A monumental 19th-century cathedral with a huge dome, marble interiors and a colonnade with city views.
places.visitorTip: Climb the colonnade for panoramas.

places.name: Nevsky Prospekt
places.description: The city’s main avenue for shopping, cafés, churches and historic city life.
places.visitorTip: Walk from the Admiralty to the Moika River.

places.name: Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg
places.description: UNESCO describes the area as a planned cultural landscape combining Baroque and Neoclassical architecture, including the Admiralty, Winter Palace and related palace complexes.
places.visitorTip: Use canal boat tours for different views.

cities.name: Kazan

seo.title: Kazan Travel Guide: Kremlin, Mosque & Tatar Culture
seo.description: Visit Kazan: the Kazan Kremlin, Qol Sharif Mosque, Bauman Street, Old Tatar Quarter and Tatar cuisine. Tips and a 2-day itinerary.
seo.h1: Kazan Travel Guide: Where Russian and Tatar Cultures Meet

cities.heading: Kazan Travel Guide: Where Russian and Tatar Cultures Meet
overview: Kazan is the capital of Tatarstan and an important meeting point of Russian, Tatar, Islamic and Orthodox cultures. It stands on the Volga River and is known for its Kremlin and food culture.
The compact centre is easy to explore on foot.

quickFacts.knownFor: Tatar and Russian culture, Kremlin, mosques, food

places.name: Kazan Kremlin
places.description: A historic fortress with both Islamic and Orthodox monuments, including the Qol Sharif Mosque, Annunciation Cathedral, defensive walls and museums.
places.visitorTip: Allow half a day and walk the walls.

places.name: Qol Sharif Mosque
places.description: A modern reconstruction of a historic Tatar mosque, opened in 2005, with large domes and minarets that symbolise Islamic cultural importance.
places.visitorTip: Dress modestly.

places.name: Bauman Street
places.description: Kazan’s main historic commercial street, with cafés, shops and churches.
places.visitorTip: Evening is lively.

places.name: Temple of All Religions
places.description: A contemporary complex with architectural references from several religions, with a visual design that reflects multi-faith themes.
places.visitorTip: Treat it as an architectural curiosity rather than an active temple.

places.name: Old Tatar Quarter
places.description: Traditional wooden houses, mosques, food and local history that preserve Tatar urban culture.
places.visitorTip: Try Tatar dishes in local cafés.

cities.name: Sochi

seo.title: Sochi Travel Guide: Black Sea Beaches & Rosa Khutor
seo.description: Explore Sochi: Black Sea beaches, Rosa Khutor, Sochi Arboretum, Olympic Park and Agur waterfalls. Tips, seasons and an itinerary.
seo.h1: Sochi Travel Guide: Black Sea Resort and Mountain Adventure

cities.heading: Sochi Travel Guide: Black Sea Resort and Mountain Adventure
overview: Sochi is a Black Sea resort city known for beaches, subtropical vegetation, mountains, wellness tourism and winter sports. It hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics.
The coast is mild in summer, while the Krasnaya Polyana mountain area offers skiing in winter and hiking in summer.

quickFacts.bestTime: June–September for beaches; December–March for skiing
quickFacts.knownFor: Black Sea beaches, Caucasus mountains, skiing, wellness

places.name: Rosa Khutor
places.description: A major Caucasus resort developed for the 2014 Olympics, with skiing, hiking, cable cars and mountain scenery.
places.visitorTip: Ride cable cars for summer views.

places.name: Sochi Arboretum
places.description: A landscaped collection of subtropical plants with garden paths and views over the city.
places.visitorTip: Allow two hours.

places.name: Sochi Olympic Park
places.description: A modern complex of stadiums and public spaces that shows the legacy of the 2014 Winter Olympics.
places.visitorTip: Visit in the evening when fountains and lights are on.

places.name: Black Sea promenade
places.description: The centre of Sochi’s resort identity with beaches, restaurants and evening walks.
places.visitorTip: Swim in summer; water is warm from July to September.

places.name: Agur Waterfalls and trails
places.description: Waterfalls and forest trails that show the contrast between the coastal resort and the Caucasus landscape.
places.visitorTip: Wear sturdy shoes.

cities.name: Vladimir and Suzdal

seo.title: Vladimir & Suzdal Travel Guide: Golden Ring Towns
seo.description: Visit Vladimir and Suzdal: white-stone churches, Golden Gate, Suzdal Kremlin and the wooden architecture museum. Tips and a 2-day itinerary.
seo.h1: Vladimir and Suzdal Travel Guide: Medieval Russia

cities.heading: Vladimir and Suzdal Travel Guide: Medieval Russia
overview: Vladimir and Suzdal are historic cities of the Golden Ring, connected with medieval Russian state formation and Orthodox architecture. Their white-stone churches are among the country’s oldest surviving monuments.
They are reached from Moscow in a few hours and give a slower cultural experience than the capitals.

quickFacts.knownFor: Golden Ring towns, white-stone churches, wooden architecture

places.name: Golden Gate of Vladimir
places.description: A 12th-century gateway that served as both a defensive and ceremonial entrance to the medieval city.
places.visitorTip: Visit with the museum for context.

places.name: Assumption Cathedral, Vladimir
places.description: Built in the 12th century, it is an important model for later Russian Orthodox cathedral design and holds frescoes.
places.visitorTip: Dress modestly.

places.name: Suzdal Kremlin
places.description: A quiet historic centre with religious buildings that represent medieval Russian urban and ecclesiastical architecture.
places.visitorTip: Walk the river embankment nearby.

places.name: Museum of Wooden Architecture
places.description: Traditional wooden churches, houses and farm buildings that preserve vernacular countryside construction.
places.visitorTip: Spend two hours exploring.

places.name: White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal
places.description: A UNESCO-listed group of monuments showing the development of Russian Orthodox architecture, including the Church of the Intercession on the Nerl.
places.visitorTip: Combine with Bogolyubovo.
